column3: Description
Small “?” or life‑ring icon that opens the main support menu.
Tiny hover/focus bubble explaining what a specific field or feature does.
Rich popover with short text, links, and “Learn more” after clicking the help icon.
Red text under an input explaining exactly why the value is invalid.
Sticky red bar listing all errors after a failed submission with anchors to each field.
Green toast stating “Saved successfully” that fades after a few seconds.
Neutral toast for non‑critical tips like “Draft autosaved.”
Yellow toast alerting users to potential issues—e.g., “Connection slow.”
Slide‑in panel containing FAQs, contact links, and live‑chat button.
Floating button that expands into a real‑time chat window with support agents.
Pre‑filled quick‑reply chips (“Reset password”, “Billing”) kicking off AI chat flows.
Autocomplete search that surfaces articles as users type.
Card or table list of help articles with categories, dates, and view counts.
Collapsible Q&A list devoted to common support questions.
Two‑column table mapping issue symptoms to quick fixes.
Paginated list of posts with tags and reply counts.
Prominent button hovering at page edge linking to ticket form.
Collects subject, category dropdown, description textarea, and file attachment.
Shows thumbnails of screenshots or logs attached to support tickets.
Displays reference number, expected response time, and “See my tickets” link.
Colored label (Open, Pending, Closed) shown in ticket lists.
Table of user’s tickets with filters for status and date.
Colored strip at top announcing downtime or degraded performance.
Embed showing real‑time uptime metrics and incident history.
Link to detailed incident report with timeline and remediation steps.
Slide‑over panel summarizing latest feature updates and fixes.
Card listing email, phone, office hours, and social support channels.
Short form scheduling a phone call with support at preferred time.
Text that updates with estimated wait (e.g., “≈ 3 minutes”).
Audio player widget users can pause during web‑call waits.
Five selectable emoji faces rating overall support experience.
Small modal popping after chat ends asking NPS or star rating.
Sticky sidebar of headings for long technical documentation.
1‑click clipboard icon on code blocks in developer docs.
Allows users to jump between v1, v2, beta documentation sets.
Link opening overlay listing all hotkeys for power users.
Footer link detailing compliance and contact process for accessibility feedback.
Tiny pill beside a menu item signaling new docs or updates.
Vertical tab labeled “Feedback” that expands into a suggestion form.
Tool letting users capture screen, draw, and send annotated bug reports directly.
